title: A.X K2 Technical Report
data_curation: Pre-training uses ~8.2T tokens, chosen from a ~16.2T candidate pool through the A.X K1 pipeline: Korean-specialized VLM PDF parsing, seed-based reasoning/agentic and topic-based knowledge synthesis, quality filtering with dedup, and PII masking with placeholder tokens. Sources were refreshed: Nemotron-CC v2.1 and Nemotron-Pretraining-Code-v2 (an English web pool of ~9.1T), a ~1.37T in-house Korean crawl, and FineWeb2. Agentic/SWE, repo-level and long-context data were expanded. A distilled A.X-Encoder classifier scores educational value and difficulty (0-4) against per-domain thresholds, using 26 web domains in Stage 1 and 14 expert domains from Stage 2. SFT data is 9.05M samples (~60.6B tokens) of paired thinking/non-thinking examples across math, science, IF, code, agent, general and safety. The safety data extends ESSA specification-guided synthesis to 50 domain-task specs with rubric filtering against over-refusal. RL rewards: rule-based IF checks; a pointwise LLM judge with reference answers over six domains and four axes; tool-call matching; and a gated judge for long-horizon agents.
curriculum: Pre-training follows a WSD schedule. Stage 1 trains 6.4T tokens at 4K context, ramping to a 2.2e-4 peak LR and a 64M-token batch. Stage 2 trains 1.4T tokens of reasoning/STEM/synthetic data while the LR cosine-decays to 7e-5. Stage 3A extends to 32K (~0.22T, RoPE base 1e4 to 1e6) and Stage 3B to 128K; Stage 3C performs SGA sparse-attention adaptation on the same mix (3B+3C ~0.14T). Instruction-format data enters during pre-training, and the last six checkpoints are merged (WSM-style). Post-training runs an indexer SFT (0.4M samples, indexer KL coefficient 0.1), then main SFT on packed 128K sequences (LR 1.5e-5, batch 128) with the indexer frozen. Multi-stage RL follows: every stage jointly trains instruction following, preference and agentic tool use, safety is added in later stages, and the data mix is re-weighted at each boundary around the weakest behaviors.
method: 688B-A33B MoE (61 layers, 256 routed experts top-8 in 8 groups, 1 shared expert, MLA, QK-norm, 163,840 vocab, 128K native/256K YaRN). Sparse Gated Attention combines a DeepSeek-style indexer selecting top-2,048 keys with a head-specific sigmoid output gate. Gated Norm (gating after RMSNorm) replaces A.X K1's dual normalization and suppresses outliers for FP8/NVFP4. Its sparse indexer warmup trains the indexer KL directly on its own top-k selection instead of dense attention. Load balancing uses a global auxiliary loss plus a learnable expert bias. Training runs in MXFP8 on 512 B200s for ~70 days. Think-Fusion SFT trains on paired thinking and non-thinking responses for the same prompt (~13:1 token ratio) so control tokens set the mode. RL uses CISPO plus GDPO per-reward normalization with a format reward and a group-relative length penalty, no KL, 16 rollouts at T=1.0, 80 prompts/batch, LR 2e-6, AdamW eps 1e-15, ~100K prompts total. Trainer and vLLM rollout both use blockwise FP8, since an MXFP8 trainer collapsed even with TIS. Rollout is asynchronous at TP1/DP8/EP8 (1.6x the throughput of TP8).
eval_metrics: Thinking-mode comparison against A.X K1, Qwen3.5-397B, Nemotron 3 Ultra, DeepSeek-V4 Flash, GLM-5.1, Kimi-K2.6 and MiniMax-M2.7 on: Math (AIME26 97.1, Apex 45.8, Apex-shortlist 88.6, KMO26 92.5); Korean (KMMLU-Pro 80.5, KoBALT 73.0, CLIcK 91.6); Code (LiveCodeBench v6 84.0, SciCode 41.0, Terminal Bench v2.1 36.0); Science/Knowledge (HLE 27.8, GPQA-D 85.6, AA-Omniscience 39.6); General (IFBench 75.9, AA-LCR 66.0); Agentic (GDPval Elo 1031, tau2-Telecom 98.0, tau3-Banking 13.0, BrowseComp 9.3). Proofs: IMO 2025 35/42 and all 8 KMO26 round-2 problems. Long context: RULER 94.6 overall to 256K, LongBench v2 63.9 (filtered), LongBench v1 62.80 dense to 62.99 sparse. In-house: KS-Eval (26 tasks), Manufacturing Benchmark (overall F1 69.0), Korean red-teaming ASR (12.1% non-thinking, 33.9% thinking). NVFP4 retains 99.0% of FP8 base accuracy.
key_results: A.X K2 leads all compared open-weight models on AIME26 (97.1), Apex (45.8, up from A.X K1's 1.0), KMMLU-Pro (80.5), CLIcK (91.6) and tau2-Telecom (98.0), and reaches IMO 2025 gold threshold (35/42), despite training on fewer tokens (~8.5T) than A.X K1 (~10T). It trails on Terminal Bench (36.0 vs up to 65.9) and BrowseComp (9.3 vs up to 29.1); sparse attention costs no LongBench quality, and NVFP4 serving gives +123.7% throughput over A.X K1 at 120K input.
evolution_note: A.X K2 is SK Telecom's successor to A.X K1 under Korea's Sovereign AI foundation model project. It combines DeepSeek-V3.2/GLM-5-style indexer sparse attention with gated attention and Gated Norm, and it simplifies the indexer warmup to a sparse-only one. Its post-training continues the hybrid-thinking line (Qwen3, DeepSeek). It replaces A.X K1's dual-track training with paired-response Think-Fusion and adopts MiniMax-M1's CISPO with GDPO multi-reward normalization. Its report that a trainer-rollout FP8 format mismatch collapses RL is practical guidance for low-precision RL on Blackwell hardware.
